sn12.24:13.2: Reverend Gotama, some ascetics and brahmins who teach the efficacy of deeds assert that suffering is made by another.
sn12.24:13.3: Reverend Gotama, some ascetics and brahmins who teach the efficacy of deeds assert that suffering is made by both oneself and another.
sn12.24:13.4: Reverend Gotama, some ascetics and brahmins who teach the efficacy of deeds assert that suffering arises anomalously, not made by oneself or another.
sn12.24:13.5: What does Venerable Gotama say about this? How does he explain it?
sn12.24:13.6: How should we answer so as to repeat what Venerable Gotama has said, and not misrepresent him with an untruth? How should we explain in line with his teaching, with no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism?’
sn12.24:14.1: When they had said this, Ānanda, I said to those wanderers of other religions:
sn12.24:14.2: ‘Reverends, I have said that suffering is dependently originated.
sn12.24:14.5: Saying this you would repeat what I have said, and not misrepresent me with an untruth. You would explain in line with my teaching, and there would be no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism.
sn12.24:15.1: Consider the ascetics and brahmins who teach the efficacy of deeds. In the case of those who assert that suffering is made by oneself, that’s dependent on contact.
sn12.24:15.4: In the case of those who assert that suffering arises anomalously, not made by oneself or another, that’s also dependent on contact.
sn12.24:16.1: Consider the ascetics and brahmins who teach the efficacy of deeds. In the case of those who assert that suffering is made by oneself, it’s impossible that they will experience that without contact.
sn12.24:16.4: In the case of those who assert that suffering arises anomalously, not made by oneself or another, it’s impossible that they will experience that without contact.’”
